clues: This big town lies at the south foot of the Alborz range, where the hills meet a high flat plain. That plain fills the heart of the land to the south.
Rain here falls mostly from late autumn to spring. The summer months are extremely dry and often pass with no rain at all.
In 1786 a king of the Qajar line picked this town as his chief town. His pick made the town the seat of rule for the whole land.
The Azadi Tower stands tall in this town as a mark of the past. It went up in 1971, for 2,500 years since the Persian realm began.
Iran is run from this town, and the work of state is done here each day. More folk live here than in any town in the whole land.
